tagline.text: Araneta City's giant 1975 wet market and its seafood paluto dining hall

location.label: Location
location.text: Araneta City, Cubao, Quezon City, 11 General Araneta Avenue

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (groceries plus cooking fees, for 1–2 people)

children.text: Farmers Market Cubao is a large wet market of about 12,000 square meters that opened in Araneta City in 1975. Fish, meat, fruit and vegetables all come together here, and the Dampa dining hall next door will cook the seafood you buy, so you can combine a Manila market tour and a meal in one visit.

Farmers Market Cubao is a large wet market inside Araneta City in the Cubao district of Quezon City, Metro Manila. It stands along General Araneta Avenue, close to EDSA, and is within walking distance of the MRT-3 Araneta Center-Cubao station. According to Wikipedia, construction began in 1974 and the building was completed and opened in early 1975. The single-floor building covers about 12,000 square meters and houses more than 50 tenants.

Despite the word "farmers" in its name, market write-ups such as Market Manila note that most vendors are not farmers selling their own harvest but middlemen who source goods from all over the country. That means you can compare vegetables and fruit from several Luzon provinces, fresh fish and meat, and even flowers all in one place. Home cooks, private chefs and restaurant buyers are regulars, so the aisles are wide and the sections are fairly well organized.

The market's history goes back to 1969, when the Coliseum Farmers Market and Shopping Center opened in what is now Farmers Plaza. The market first occupied the lower ground floor of that building and moved to its present site in 1975. ACI Inc. owns the market building, and the Quezon City government monitors its hygiene and operations. Wikipedia reports that it is in the Quezon City Cleanest Market Hall of Fame.

For travelers, it has two faces. One is the everyday life of locals shopping, where you can watch people choosing fish and vegetables from dawn. The other is Dampa sa Farmers Market next to the market. You can take seafood and meat bought in the market to a paluto (cook-it-for-you restaurant), pay a cooking fee and eat on the spot, which makes it a great way to experience a Filipino seafood meal. Famous chefs such as Anthony Bourdain are also said to have featured this market.

On beds of ice you will see local fish such as galunggong, talakitok and lapu-lapu. Market Manila also mentioned tuna and six kinds of seaweed. The varieties and prices change every day, so it pays to walk around a few stalls before choosing.
This section keeps live fish in freshwater tanks. You can have the fish you pick cleaned right away and take it to be cooked, which makes it popular with people who care most about freshness.

This is a paluto dining hall that cooks the ingredients you bring from the market. On top of the price of the ingredients, a cooking fee per kilogram is added, and you choose a method such as soup, grilled or fried. Wikipedia notes that Restaurant Guru recommended it in 2023.

Market Manila says the upper level sells vegetables, fruit and flowers, and singled out small sweet Korean squash, deep orange sweet potatoes, baby corn and leafy greens. Local and imported fruit are mixed together, which makes it a good place to try tropical fruit.
Besides the usual cuts of pork, beef and chicken, some stalls are said to sell goat meat and live native chickens. If you want to eat what you buy, you can ask Dampa to cook it for you.
Inside the market you will find general merchandise shops, a barbershop, a hair salon, bakeries, fast-food outlets and a Mercury Drug pharmacy. You can pick up medicine or a snack while you shop.
Wikipedia reports that the market introduced online transactions and cashless payment during COVID-19. Each shop accepts different methods, however, so it is safer to bring some cash.
The MRT-3 and LRT-2 Cubao stations are close, and Gateway Mall, Smart Araneta Coliseum and Manhattan Gardens are nearby, so it is easy to add shopping or a show after your market visit.

items.title: Early-morning market tour
items.subtitle: Pick fresh ingredients and have a paluto breakfast

children.text: Get off at the MRT-3 Araneta Center-Cubao station and walk toward Farmers Plaza to enter the market. The market opens at 4 AM, so business is already in full swing early in the morning.
Start with the vegetable, fruit and flower section to get a feel for the market. The earlier you come, the wider the choice and the less crowded the aisles.
Compare prices at two or three stalls in the fish and seafood section. Decide how much you want and watch it being weighed at the stall.
Carry your seafood to the Dampa dining hall, choose a cooking method and check the cooking-fee board.
After eating, browse the bakeries and shops in the market for snacks and food items that make good souvenirs, then wrap up.
The market itself runs from early morning, but opening hours at the Dampa dining hall differ from shop to shop. If you want to eat early, check first that the shop is open.

items.title: Half-day Cubao route
items.subtitle: Market visit and a walk around Araneta City

children.text: Arrive at the market and walk a full lap of the aisles to learn where each section is.
Look over the Fishmoko live-fish section and the meat counters, and decide what to eat for lunch.
Have the ingredients cooked at Dampa and eat them for lunch. Check the cooking fee and service charge before you order.
Walk around other parts of Araneta City, such as Farmers Plaza and Gateway Mall.
Drop by the market again before closing to buy fruit and vegetables to take home, or head to the MRT-3 or LRT-2 station to return.
Take the MRT-3 along EDSA from Ayala station in Makati or from the southern part of Manila, and get off at Araneta Center-Cubao station.
From the station you can walk past Farmers Plaza to the market. According to Wikipedia, the market is north of the station.
Fares and operating hours can change, so check the latest announcements.
From northern Manila or the Marikina side, use the LRT-2 Araneta Center-Cubao station.
The LRT-2 station is in the northeast of Araneta City, so it is a slightly longer walk than from the MRT-3 station.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) you can reach Cubao by taxi or ride-hailing car. Travel time depends heavily on EDSA traffic, so check locally.
To save time, avoid weekday rush hours when EDSA is badly congested.
Farmers Plaza has a UV Express terminal, and EDSA bus stops are close by. Wikipedia reports that Antipolo-bound buses stop at the Farmers Plaza bus stop below the MRT concourse.
If you drive, there are about 100 parking slots along Central Avenue by the market. Market Manila reports that the parking lot fills up later in the day.

The market operates year-round, but the best time to visit is early morning. There is more to choose from and the aisles are quieter, so it is easier to walk around. On weekend afternoons, by contrast, it is said to get crowded and busy.
During the Philippine rainy season (June–November) the market building keeps you out of the rain, but the walk to it can get wet. Bring an umbrella or rain jacket.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Less heat makes this the most comfortable time to stroll the market.
It is hot during the day. Early morning or evening visits are better.
The building shelters you from rain, but getting around can be inconvenient, so check the weather forecast.

Cubao is a transport hub where EDSA, the MRT-3 and the LRT-2 meet, so it is easy to reach from anywhere in Manila, not just from near the market. There are hotels of various sizes in and around Araneta City, so compare reviews and locations to suit your schedule. If the market tour is your goal, a day trip from Makati or Ortigas is perfectly enough without staying overnight in Cubao.

For food, Dampa sa Farmers Market is the clear choice. Take the fish, shrimp and clams you picked at the market and ask for them to be cooked as soup (sinigang), grilled or fried. Each shop has a minimum order, and a cooking fee and service charge may be added on top of the ingredient price, so ask for the total before you order. The market also has bakeries and fast-food outlets for a lighter bite.
The market opens early in the morning. Go early if you want fresh ingredients and plenty of choice.
Watch your seafood being weighed, and it is better to ask the price at one or two more stalls before deciding.
At Dampa, always ask about the cooking fee, the minimum order and whether the service charge is included before ordering.
The market floor can be wet, so wear non-slip shoes.
Bring plenty of small cash. Each shop accepts electronic payment differently.
According to Market Manila, the vegetable and fruit section upstairs is cleaner than the seafood and meat section downstairs. The seafood area can be untidy depending on garbage collection times.
Parking tends to fill up later in the day, so arrive early if you drive.
Fresh groceries are hard to carry around for long, so make the market your last stop or bring a cooler box.
Pickpockets can operate in crowded markets, so carry your bag in front and watch your phone and wallet.
Check seafood freshness with your own eyes, and do not buy it if in doubt.
Some shops may quote a higher price to tourists who do not know the going rate. Confirm the price after the item is weighed.

Opening hours differ by day and by shop. Check the latest announcements before you visit. According to Araneta Group, the market is open Monday to Saturday from 4 AM to 7 PM, and until 6 PM on Sunday.
EDSA and the Cubao area are extremely congested during weekday rush hours. Allow extra time to get around.
Groceries left at room temperature for a long time can spoil, so cook them right after buying or keep them refrigerated.
